title: Deployment mini-docket: launch protocol and timeline (Jun 2026) - WIP
body:
Purpose: compact 1-pager mini-docket for the June 2026 feature launch. This is intentionally short — use during the 48hr window as the single source of truth for operations, owners, and immediate rollback criteria.

SUMMARY
- What: feature rollout for adaptive-batching + new model-kv-cache tuning (internal flag: adaptive_batch_v2).
- Why: 15-25% token cost reduction in blend workloads while preserving 95th pct latency SLOs.
- Scope: hosted API + dedicated pools; Private deployments not part of this rollout.
- Risk level: medium (new kernel selection path + config toggle).

PRE-FLIGHT (72->0 hours) - owners in parens
- Confirm PR merges are green and no unexpected approvals pending (Aisha).
- Tag and publish deploy artifacts (runtime image + config bundle) and store SHA in release tag (Marcus).
- Smoke test matrix: small/medium/large sequence lengths + convo replay on staging (Lena).
- Load test: run 1h blended synthetic at 20% prod RPS, verify p50/p95/p99 latency within thresholds (Ravi).
- Telemetry hooks: ensure new metrics emitted (kv_cache_hits, batch_size_dist) and dashboards have alert rules bound (Joanne).
- Feature flag gating: staged rollout flag (adaptive_batch_v2) created in FF service and feature flag file uploaded to release bundle (Aisha).
- Capacity ops: confirm spare GPU pools reserved for rollback scaling (infra-oncall).
- Migration notes: none (no DB/schema changes).
- Stakeholder signoff: product + privacy checked (product: Lena; privacy: Joanne).

48HR ROLLOUT CALENDAR (UTC) - condensed
Day -2 (T-48h): finalize artifacts, ship canary config, notify on #release-ops. (Aisha)
Day -1 (T-24h): run extended smoke & soak test for 6h, preflight RC signoff at 17:00 UTC. (Marcus, Lena)
Day 0 (T=0): start canary step 1 at 09:00 UTC — 2% traffic for 30m. Health evaluation at 09:30. (Ravi)
Day 0 (T+2h): canary step 2 at 11:00 UTC — 10% traffic for 1h. Health evaluation at 12:10. (Ravi)
Day 0 (T+6h): step 3 at 15:00 UTC — 50% traffic for 2h. If healthy, full release at 17:30. (Marcus)
Day 0 (T+12h): Post-release monitoring window (24h heightened telemetry). (All)

CANARY HEALTH GATES (explicit metrics to check)
- Request error rate (5xx) increase: absolute >0.5% or relative >2x baseline -> FAIL. (auto alert + manual check)
- p95 latency: degradation >20% absolute or >150ms -> FAIL.
- CUDA OOM or process restarts: any occurrence -> FAIL (immediate rollback).
- kv_cache_hit_ratio: regress >10% relative to baseline -> investigate (non-blocking unless coupled with latency).
- Token throughput (tokens/sec): should not drop >15% vs baseline -> investigate.

ROLLBACK TRIGGERS & ACTIONS
- Trigger: any CANARY HEALTH GATE marked FAIL.
- Immediate action: set adaptive_batch_v2 flag OFF globally, pause rollout, scale down new image, alert on-call. (Owner: Aisha)
- Secondary action: revert to previous runtime image and clear in-flight queues as per rollback playbook. (Owner: Marcus)
- Post-rollback: incident postmortem within 72h; tag all related traces and collect sample prompts for QA. (Owner: Ravi)

COMMUNICATION & ESCALATION
- Primary comms channel: #release-ops (use prefix "[LAUNCH-Jun2026]").
- Exec updates: send canned status at major milestones (canary start, canary pass, full release). Template below. (Joanne)
- Pager: infra-oncall for node issues; app-sre for runtime regressions; eng-release-engineering for orchestration.
- Stakeholder notice: product, PMM, SalesOps via email at full release completion.

POST-DEPLOY VALIDATION (T+0 -> T+24h)
- Synthetic checks: run traffic replays for 3 key customers and verify output parity within tolerance (Lena).
- Quality eval: run prompt set (n=200) and compare top-1 generation quality metrics to baseline; flag any >5% regression. (Ravi)
- Cost telemetry: confirm per-token compute spend aligns with expected -10% to -20% band. (Marcus)
- Observability: ensure dashboards show stable ingestion and no gaps in spans/logs. (Joanne)

RELEASE NOTES - DRAFT (short, for external/internal)
Title: Adaptive batching and KV-cache tuning (adaptive_batch_v2)
Summary: Deployed a new adaptive batching runtime path that reduces token compute costs in mixed-length workloads and improves cache utilization. Users should see reduced cost per token with comparable latency for typical usage patterns.
User impact: no migration required. Some customers with extreme single-token bursts may see different latency profiles — we are monitoring.
Known issues: under very high short-sequence burst scenarios, p50 latency could increase slightly; we will follow up with a targeted micro-optimization.
Contact: eng-release-engineering@redwood.ai for any performance regressions or unexpected failures.

RISKS & MITIGATIONS (quick register)
- Kernel selector bug: mitigation = keep fast rollback image + enable verbose kernel logging for 2h post-rollout.
- Telemetry gaps: mitigation = parallel synthetic probes and sidecar logging to S3.
- Customer-facing regressions: mitigation = quick opt-out flag and customer-notify playbook.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOS (notes to self)
- Confirm alert owner is subscribed to #release-ops for the window (Joanne).
- Add one-line snippet to show how to flip feature flag from CLI (Marcus).
- Validate private deployment exclusion path — add explicit exclusion test tomorrow.

APPENDIX: canned status template for Slack (copy/paste)
- [LAUNCH-Jun2026] Canary step 1 started (2% traffic). Owners: Ravi + Marcus. Live checks: p95, 5xx, OOMs. ETA next check: 09:30 UTC.
- [LAUNCH-Jun2026] Canary step 1 PASS. Proceeding to 10% at 11:00 UTC.

---
This doc is a working mini-docket: keep it short and actionable. If anything in the plan changes, append a one-line change log with timestamp and name.

Change log:
- 2026-06-10 Aisha: created initial mini-docket.
- 2026-06-12 Marcus: added canary percent cadence and rollback triggers.
- 2026-06-15 Lena: updated telemetry checklist and post-deploy validation steps.
